name: thc-scene
tagline: A live terminal UI, as one JSON value an agent drives

license.notes: Same as thc. The scene crate is on a prototype branch and not yet published.

backing: One author (Thought Control), with agents doing much of the building.

notable_users: thc itself (its Today screen, rebuilt cell for cell)
adoption.summary: Unreleased. Used only in demos so far: a thc Today rebuild, a finance dashboard, stress tests and a pixel tour.

maintainability.recent_activity: Built in October 2026 on a branch of thought-control.
maintainability.summary: A prototype with tests and measured numbers, but one person and no release.

architecture.summary: The whole UI is one serializable value: a tree of components, data sources bound to shell commands, JSON-line streams or literals, keys, a theme and callout layers. Elm architecture: a serializable State, a pure update that returns effects, a pure view that returns the frame plus hit regions and pictures. A runtime owns the terminal, a local control socket, child processes and the pixel layer. It sits on caretline (a Helix-model editing engine) and caretline-layers (placement for callouts, arrows and spotlights).
key_points: Push a whole UI, or patch one node by id; view state (selection, focus) survives by id, like React keys
Read the current frame as text, or the full state, from outside
Keys, mouse and clicks injected like a person's
`upgrade`: the running screen saves its state, execs a new binary and carries on
Templates with theme-token styles, value maps and conditionals; data values can't inject styles
Kitty graphics: cards beneath text, anti-aliased plots, SVG rendered with resvg, PNGs; cells everywhere else

claims.text: About 6,000 whole-UI pushes a second from one client while drawing ~108 fps (release build, 170×52).
1,000 patches a second applied with every frame under 1 ms; a 50,000-row list replaced 20 times a second draws in 0.18 ms.
With a 15 Hz pixel plot, frames take ~7 ms: rasterising on the main thread. Not yet moved to a worker.

performance.summary: Measured by its own stress suite on one machine; not independently reproduced.

agent_usability.how: A local Unix socket with JSON-line requests: push, patch, key, mouse, click, layers, screen, state, stats, upgrade. A CLI wraps each one. No MCP server yet.
agent_usability.integration_effort: Write one JSON UI and point its sources at commands; send ops over the socket. An MCP server is the planned way in for any agent.
agent_usability.readback: Yes: `screen` (the frame as text) and `state` (everything, as JSON).
agent_usability.granular_edits: Yes: `patch` replaces one node by id; streams update one source; keys and clicks move selections.
agent_usability.history: Not yet. State is serializable and every input is a message, so it's designed (history, state_at, screen_at, diff, seek, fork, replay, export/import) but not built.
agent_usability.summary: Built for agents to drive and to see. The parts a standard would give it (MCP, A2UI input) are missing.

score_notes.time_travel: 0 today. Planned: an agent can read, seek, fork and replay (see the design).
score_notes.teaching: Callouts, spotlights and scripted tours work today; record, take over and rewind are planned.
score_notes.pixel_graphics: Rich, but only where the terminal speaks the kitty graphics protocol (Ghostty, kitty, iTerm2, VS Code)
score_notes.maturity: A prototype: one author, no release.
score_notes.openness: MIT, but single-author and not yet published.

steelman: The best case: an agent can write a terminal UI as one small JSON value, drive it like a person, see exactly what it drew, change one piece at a time, and keep live data flowing at thousands of updates a second without that data ever passing through the model. It has already reproduced a hand-written production screen cell for cell, so a generated UI doesn't have to look generated. Nothing else found pairs that loop with a terminal-native renderer and a pixel layer.
weaknesses: A prototype by one author, unreleased, untested by anyone else.
Its own format: no A2UI, json-render or MCP Apps input yet, against standards with real momentum.
Data sources run shell commands: the opposite of the field's 'data, not code' safety stance. Needs a command policy before anyone pushes untrusted UIs.
Fullscreen only: loses the terminal's native scrollback, search and selection, which agent CLIs have been moving back toward.
Pixel features need kitty-graphics terminals (a minority).
No MCP server yet, so agents need the socket or the CLI.

relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Declarative UI formats (A2UI, json-render), terminal rendering (ratatui underneath), patch protocols (JSON Patch).
borrow: A2UI's updateComponents and JSON Patch as input
LangGraph's checkpoint vocabulary and Redux DevTools' verbs for time travel
Rerun's split between a view written once and data streamed at high rates
relation_to_scene.gap_left: A live UI that an agent writes, drives, reads back and will be able to rewind: one value, terminal-native, fed by streams that bypass the model.
